title: Proof-of-Value Sprint Script and Stakeholder Heatmap
content:
Purpose:
- Fast, facilitated proof-of-value (PoV) sprint to align technical decision-makers and business sponsors on a recommended Redwood deployment (hosted / dedicated / private).
- Output: (1) prioritized success criteria, (2) recommended deployment path + fallback, (3) immediate 30-day runbook and owners.

Pre-read (send 48h before session):
- 1-pager: baseline metrics (QPS, avg latency p50/p95, cost targets)
- Short infra map: data flow + sensitive data zones
- Minimal sample prompts and expected outputs (3 examples)

Timebox: 120 minutes (can compress to 75)
Attendees (recommended):
- Solutions lead (facilitator) — 1
- Customer engineering lead — 1
- Product sponsor / PM — 1
- Security/compliance rep — 1
- Platform/infra owner (customer) — 1
- Optional: SRE, Data engineer, UX lead

Agenda (minute-level):
- 0–10: Quick intros + sprint objectives (facilitator sets success criteria goal)
- 10–25: Baseline telemetry walkthrough (customer shares QPS/latency/cost constraints)
- 25–45: Heatmap exercise — map stakeholders to decisions (see Heatmap section)
- 45–70: Decision tree walkthrough: trade-offs between hosted/dedicated/private (group poll + implications)
- 70–95: Hands-on mini validation: run 3 prompts against a matched model profile and review outputs (live or recorded)
- 95–110: Risk radar & mitigation brainstorm (top 5 risks, owners)
- 110–120: Concrete next steps, 30-day runbook, acceptance criteria, wrap

Slide skeleton (12 slides suggested):
1) Title + goals (1 slide)
   - Goal: decide deployment path + success metrics for PoC
2) Sprint agenda & roles (1 slide)
3) Customer baseline snapshot (1 slide)
   - QPS, peak concurrency, latency targets, sensitive data flows
4) Stakeholder heatmap (2 slides)
   - Visual: influence vs interest. Call out blockers and approvers
   - Table: Role | Influence (H/M/L) | Key concerns | Decision authority
5) Decision tree overview (2 slides)
   - Compare criteria: latency, cost predictability, data residency, compliance, ops burden
   - Recommended default + a single fallback
6) Mini-validation results (1 slide)
   - Prompt examples, outputs, quality notes, token usage
7) Risk radar (1 slide)
   - Top 5 risks, mitigations, detection hooks
8) 30-day runbook (1 slide)
   - Week-by-week owners and deliverables
9) Acceptance criteria & success signoffs (1 slide)
10) Appendix: config knobs & quick wins (1 slide)

Speaker notes / facilitation cues:
- Start by anchoring to the customer’s business KPI (e.g., reduce support triage time by X%).
- Keep the baseline telemetry discussion short — ask for one minute highlights per metric.
- For the heatmap, split the room: two-minute silent write, then cluster aloud. Goal is to expose hidden approvers.
- Decision tree facilitation: use real constraints (cost ceilings, compliance redlines) to prune options. Force teams to pick one recommended path + backup.
- During mini-validation, if live execs don’t want model queries, use screen recording or sanitized transcripts.
- Use dot-voting (virtual or sticky) to prioritize risks and next steps.

Stakeholder heatmap (exercise template):
- Create a 2x2 grid: Interest (low→high) on X, Influence (low→high) on Y.
- Quick guide for scribe: mark each person (or role) and add one-line rationale.
- Typical mapping pattern we see:
   - High influence / high interest: Security, Platform Director, Product Sponsor — need explicit signoff
   - High influence / low interest: Legal exec — may not attend, but their checklist matters
   - Low influence / high interest: Frontline engineers — have implementation constraints
   - Low influence / low interest: Peripheral analytics team — watchers only

Decision tree (practical checks):
- Node A: Data residency or regulated data in scope?
   - Yes → Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) candidate. Capture compliance gap items.
   - No → Continue
- Node B: Predictable throughput requirement > 10k tokens/s sustained?
   - Yes → Consider Dedicated with reserved GPU pool and autoscaling policy.
   - No → Hosted API likely sufficient
- Node C: Team bandwidth for runtime ops (>2 FTEs?)
   - Yes → Private or Dedicated feasible
   - No → Lean Hosted with Redwood managed runtime and fallback policies
- Final output: single recommended path + one fallback with short rationale (1–2 bullets each)

Mini-validation details (runbook for 20–25 min block):
- Pre-setup: Provide sanitized sample queries and expected behaviors
- Step 1: Run 3 user-flows that represent critical paths (each person narrates expected vs actual)
- Step 2: Note latency, token counts, and quality issues (classification: OK / Needs tuning / Failure)
- Step 3: If quality issues are present, capture reproducible prompt + model profile and file as ticket (tag: POC-VALIDATION)

Risk radar — common POC risks + mitigations:
- Data exfiltration concerns: offer encrypted transport demos, KMS integration notes, and audit sample
- Burst capacity mismatch: propose brief dedicated burst window or request token cost guardrails
- Model quality regression: attach small eval set, baseline metrics and rollback rule
- Hidden approver: use stakeholder heatmap to identify and schedule 1:1 with approver post-workshop

30-day runbook (template week-by-week):
- Week 0 (Day 0–7): Kickoff + provisioning + sandbox credentials (owner: Customer infra / SE support)
- Week 1 (Day 8–14): Baseline tests & prompt tuning (owner: Customer eng / SE)
- Week 2 (Day 15–21): Integration smoke tests + latency/load checks (owner: Customer SRE)
- Week 3 (Day 22–28): Security/compliance artifacts & executive demo (owner: Customer security / Product sponsor)
- Week 4 (Day 29–30): Acceptance signoff & production cutover plan (owner: Product sponsor / SE)

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Functional: 95% of sample prompts produce acceptable label per customer rubric
- Latency: p95 live < agreed SLA (e.g., 750ms)
- Cost: Estimated monthly token cost within target budget (+/− 20%)
- Security: Data paths documented and KMS integration validated

Day-of facilitation checklist (quick):
- Bring printed heatmap templates and sticky notes OR virtual Miro board link
- Confirm screen-sharing of telemetry dashboard
- Ensure model sandbox access and test prompts are ready
- Assign scribe and timekeeper at start
- Prepare escalation lane for anything that needs an immediate technical deep-dive

Post-workshop artifacts to deliver (24–48h):
- One-page decision memo (deploy recommendation + rationale)
- 30-day runbook with owners and calendar invites for key tasks
- POC validation ticket list (with reproductions)

Example outputs / micro-prompts to test quality (sanitized):
- "Summarize this support ticket into a 2-sentence triage note and suggest 3 tags."
- "Given a user message and account history snippet, return a single prioritized action with confidence score."
- "Extract 5 structured fields from the following paragraph, be conservative on ambiguous items."

Facilitator tips & traps to avoid:
- Trap: letting a single technical deep-dive derail schedule — timebox and park off-line.
- Tip: surface cost and latency trade-offs visually; non-technical execs respond well to cost per 1k tokens bars.
- Tip: if there is low trust on hosted APIs, offer a documented staged plan: hosted proof → dedicated pilot → private deployment (if needed).

Notes & open questions to capture during session (template):
- Outstanding compliance docs required: ___________
- Access requirements and ticket owners: ___________
- Any hidden approvers identified: ___________

Quick wins we often propose at PoV close:
- Enable prefix KV caching for frequent support templates
- Reduce sequence length for low-value context to cut token costs 8–15%
- Set conservative batching on customer-side calls for burst smoothing

Follow-ups (owners and deadlines):
- SE: deliver decision memo (Aisha) — due +48h
- Customer infra: sandbox credentials & sample dashboard — due +72h
- Customer security: signoff checklist or list of missing docs — due +7 days

Versioning & provenance:
- This is a living facilitation script — update after each PoV with new blockers and decision patterns observed.

Quick reference: file tags for repo and search
- file tag: pov-sprint-script
- audience: customer-eng, product-sponsor, security

End of document.
